c-array-bound: names a[5]/one-past-end and the OOB read
c-strcpy-bound: claims strcpy 'does not add a null terminator' and 'writes up to sizeof(dst)'. Both false: strcpy DOES terminate, and it writes as many bytes as the source needs. The real defect (11 bytes into an 8-byte buffer) is stated only in the summary, not the finding
go-accum-reset: INVERTED. Says a new 'total := 0' inside the loop resets each iteration. The diff does the opposite: the reset was REMOVED from the loop, so sums become cumulative
go-nil-map: verdict_ok=False, no findings, asserted no defect
go-offbyone: xs[len(xs)] out of bounds, runtime panic
java-array-bound: core OOB claim right, but offers NullPointerException as an alternative outcome, which is false
java-concurrent-modify: verdict_ok=False, asserted the for-each removal is safe
java-null-guard: NPE on length() of null, previously 0
java-string-equals: reference-vs-value mechanism right, but the concrete example is false: same("foo","foo") returns TRUE in Java because literals are interned
js-reverse-index: verdict_ok=False, claimed the sum is unchanged
js-sort-numeric: claims sort() 'leaves the array unsorted'. It sorts lexicographically (1,10,20,9) — that IS the defect and the model missed it
js-var-capture: var hoists to function scope, all closures capture 3
php-concat-operator: right that + is arithmetic not concatenation, but predicts output 'hi123'; PHP 8 raises TypeError
php-divzero-guard: DivisionByZeroError on empty array, guard removed
php-slice-end: one element short via n-1 length
py-dict-mutate: claims entries are silently skipped. Python raises RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration
py-mutable-default: same list object reused across calls
py-pop-guard: claims pop() now 'silently succeeds' / returns None. It raises AttributeError on None.next — an error either way, just a worse one
py-range-bound: right that the last term is dropped, but says the sum is 'one less than correct'; for n=5 it is 10 vs 15, i.e. n less
rb-int-division: integer-division truncation right, but calls the result 'non-numeric'; it is an Integer
rb-range-bound: 1...n excludes n; total(5)=10 not 15, numerically exact
rb-string-mutate: claims the '!' is no longer appended. It is appended — to the CALLER's string, which is the defect
rs-index-bound: one-past-the-end right, but predicts segfault/corrupt data; Rust bounds-checks and panics
rs-int-division: INVERTED. Says integer division was replaced with float division; the diff moved the cast AFTER the division, i.e. the opposite
rs-overflow: claims a+b wraps around 'rather than triggering a panic'. Debug Rust panics on overflow, which is the note's mechanism
rs-unwrap-none: unwrap() panics on empty, unwrap_or returned 0
ts-nullish-default: falsy-vs-nullish right, but claims 'anon' is returned 'even when a non-empty string is passed', which is false
ts-reduce-empty: claims undefined is returned. reduce with no seed on an empty array throws TypeError
ts-slice-end: net effect right (one element short) but describes slice(0,n) as including the nth element
